as_told.title: Bahnson funds T. Townsend Brown's gravity experiments

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1950s a North Carolina man named Agnew Bahnson, head of a research group called the Institute of Field Physics, was paying for the work of an inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels says Brown was building "gravitator" devices meant to control gravity, worked on them at the back of Bahnson's house, and claimed positive results, and that Bahnson said strange things happened there. If true, it would mean serious private money was backing early efforts to control gravity.
